pages.raw_text: API Reference / Overview API Reference Overview REST APIs for memory management, search, entity operations, and persistent context. The Negentro REST API provides programmatic access to persistent memory and context operations, allowing applications and agents to create, retrieve, search, update, and manage memory through standard HTTP requests. API VERSION v1 BASE URL Configure in your deployment → Quick start Get your API key and make your first memory request in a few minutes. Get API key → Quick Start Guide 01 Add Memories Store information and context from your application's conversations or events. See Add Memories → 02 Search Memories Retrieve relevant memories using semantic or contextual search. See Search Memories → 03 Get Memories Retrieve a specific stored memory when you already know its identifier. See Get Memories → Bash POST Create a memory Copy curl -X POST "https://<your-negentro-api>/v1/memories" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $NEGENTRO_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"user_id": "user_123", "content": "User prefers concise explanations"}' Core Operations + POST Add Memories Store new memories from conversations and interactions. /v1/memories → POST Search Memories Find relevant memories using semantic search and filters. /v1/memories/search → PATCH Update Memory Modify existing memory content or metadata. /v1/memories/:id → DELETE Delete Memory Remove a specific memory or perform supported deletion operations. /v1/memories/:id → API Categories Explore the API by functionality. Memory APIs Core memory operations including create, search, update, delete, history, and export workflows. Events APIs Track and inspect asynchronous memory-related events. Entities APIs Manage users, agents, applications, and associated memory data. Organizations & Projects Manage organization-level access, projects, and collaboration boundaries. Webhooks Receive real-time notifications for supported memory and system events. Building a multi-tenant application? Learn how Organizations & Projects can be used to separate access, resources, and collaboration boundaries. Organizations & Projects → Authentication All requests to the Negentro API must include a valid API key passed via the Authorization header using the Bearer scheme. Requests without a valid key will be rejected. Header Copy Authorization: Bearer <NEGENTRO_API_KEY> API keys should be stored server-side Requests should be made through secure server-side environments Do not expose secrets in client-side code JavaScript Copy const response = await fetch ( "https://<your-negentro-api>/v1/memories" , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.NEGENTRO_API_KEY}` } } ) Your Application HTTP Request Negentro API Memory / Context Layer Response Keep your API key secure. Never expose API credentials in client-side code or public repositories. Use environment variables and server-side requests. Next Steps + Add your first memory Start storing persistent context through the API. → Search with filters Learn advanced search and filtering techniques. → Build with cookbooks See complete API workflows inside practical projects. → Suggest edits Raise issue ← Previous Cookbooks Next → Organizations & Projects →

pages.title: Add Memories
pages.breadcrumb: API Reference / Core Memory Operations / Add Memories
pages.lead: Store new information, agent interactions, and bitemporal facts into persistent memory.

sections.heading: Add Memories
paragraphs: Store new information, agent interactions, and bitemporal facts into persistent memory.

curl -X POST https://api.piyapi.cloud/api/v1/memories \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $PIYAPI_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "content": "Client requested SOC2 Type II compliance audit report for Q3 2026.", "tags": ["compliance", "soc2", "audit"], "metadata": { "client_id": "cli_8812", "urgency": "high" }, "valid_at": "2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z" }' Response Schema (201 Created):

code_blocks.title: POST /api/v1/memories LIVE VERIFIED Copy
code_blocks.code:
curl -X POST https://api.piyapi.cloud/api/v1/memories \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PIYAPI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "content": "Client requested SOC2 Type II compliance audit report for Q3 2026.",
    "tags": ["compliance", "soc2", "audit"],
    "metadata": { "client_id": "cli_8812", "urgency": "high" },
    "valid_at": "2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  }'

code_blocks.title: POST /api/v1/search Copy
code_blocks.code:
curl -X POST https://api.piyapi.cloud/api/v1/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PIYAPI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "query": "SOC2 audit report requests",
    "limit": 5,
    "alpha": 0.7,
    "tags": ["compliance"],
    "min_score": 0.25
  }'
